newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares had a healthy Thursday and ended firmly in positive territory after being helped by a firmer gold sector and a bullish short-term outlook for major international markets, dealers said.
The bullion price -- which on Wednesday hit its lowest level since October 4, 1993 -- rallied slightly and dragged South Africa's bombed out gold shares up with it.
Industrial shares had a firmer day on the back of healthy demand for a wide-range of stocks, especially blue-chips, and a bullish outlook for major international markets.

London shares rose further into record territory by early afternoon as a rise in U.S. treasury bonds pointed to a higher opening on Wall Street after profit-taking on Wednesday ended a recent surge in New York.
"It has been a good strong day across the board and if Wall Street is up tonight we should have another good day tomorrow," one dealer said.
The all-share index rose 27.6 points to finish at 6,779 as the industrials index jumped 45.7 points to 8,176.4.

Most blue-chips posted gains with SA Breweries up 175 cents to 125.50 and De Beers gaining 50 cents to 135.50. Volumes were healthy with 706 million rands worth of shares changing hands, though dealers said about 100 million rands of that was in the form of corporate finance deals.
Some of the strongest performers of the day were in smaller stocks with Energy Africa Ltd gaining well after a recent exploration deal in Gabon.

Analysts said the firm's small size would give it a cost-advantage over its larger competitors. "Some of the fields have been known for some time, but have not been developed because they have been considered uneconomic by the oil majors," said Themis Themistocleous, an analyst at brokerage SBC Warburg.
The firm ended the day up 200 cents to 20.50 rand.

Gold shares had a good day with the index rising just under percent, or 12.6 points, to 1,421 as the first day of the quarterly reporting season kicked off with Goldfields announcing healthy third quarter results.
Goldfields ended the day unchanged at 119 rand, Kloof put on 20 cents to 35.05 rand and Driefontein rose 30 cents to 44 rand.
In the futures market contracts strenghtened after a bout of arbitrage early in the day when dealers sold futures to buy stocks.

In late trade the all-share March contract had risen to 6,310/20 from 6,270 as the industrials contract jumped to 8,055/62 from 7,973. The gold contract dipped, however, and was at 1,010/20 from 1,033.
